newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates slip, market eyes Euro outcome.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates slip, market eyes Euro outcome.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were fractionally lower on Tuesday and dealers said only a few participants were entering the market as the yield curve remained flat and the market was worried about EMU prospects.
Dealers said, however, that a postponement of the introduction of the Euro and the creation of European monetary union would not be all that bad for the Netherlands and Germany.
"Investors might flee into safe currencies like the Dutch guilder and the German mark," said one dealer.
He added that this could press rates somewhat lower in Germany and the Netherlands.
Another dealer said rates in Germany and the Netherlands were unlikely to fall much as they were already at a very low level.
"But Germany and the Netherlands could certainly be safe havens for investors in case the uncertainty on the Euro continues," he said.
Call money rates were some six basis points lower at 3.06 percent bid. Deposits up to six months slipped two basis points, with three month deposits trading at 3.18 percent bid.
The guilder was trading at 112.495 per 100 marks from 112.505 on Monday.
